title: Warp markers of yours change the compiled timeline; explain names the grid
description:
## Behavior
```gherkin
Feature: Your warp markers win over the analysis grid

  Background:
    Given the analyzed fixture sample "steady-120.wav" whose analysis puts beat 8 at 4.500 s
    And the score "steady.apr" plays "steady-120.wav" beats 0..16 at tempo 120

  Scenario: Without warp markers of yours the analysis grid is used
    When I compile "steady.apr"
    Then the first event's warp map pins 4.500 s to beat 8

  Scenario: Your warp markers change the compiled timeline
    Given my warp markers on "steady-120.wav" put beat 8 at 4.600 s and keep every other beat where the analysis has it
    When I compile "steady.apr"
    Then the first event's warp map pins 4.600 s to beat 8

  Scenario: Beyond your last marker the last segment's tempo continues
    Given my warp markers on "steady-120.wav" cover only beats 0 to 8
    When I compile "steady.apr"
    Then beats 9 to 16 follow the tempo between my last two markers

  Scenario: A tempo change in the middle of a bar
    Given my warp markers on "tempo-change.wav" include one at beat 6.5
    When I compile a score playing it beats 4..8
    Then the event's warp map has a point at beat 6.5 of the clip

  Scenario: explain says which grid a clip used
    Given my warp markers on "steady-120.wav"
    When I run "apricity explain steady.apr"
    Then the clip's lines include "grid: yours (18 warp markers)"
```
